headline: High-risk shared filesystem and MCP create prompt-injection, leakage, and write-conflict pathways; Roo Code’s default workspace access makes the pair unsafe without isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can use MCP and consumes files/APIs, while Roo Code also uses MCP and reads/writes VS Code workspace files. That creates a plausible instruction-smuggling path if Roo Code writes attacker-controlled content into shared files or MCP outputs that OpenBBTerminal treats as trusted. The pathway is not proven by docs alone, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Roo Code writes model-generated text into a file or MCP resource that OpenBBTerminal later parses as instructions
IF both agents are connected to the same MCP server without provenance tagging
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different workspaces or directories
Disable MCP on one side for the shared task
Require a human review step before OpenBBTerminal consumes any Roo Code output
Use read-only mounts for any shared files
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to MCP/file outputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial, licensed, and public data, and Roo Code has broad filesystem read/write plus browser screenshots. If they share a workspace, Roo Code can read sensitive files OpenBBTerminal produces or caches, and its configured model API can transmit that context externally. The shared-workspace plus upload path fits medium severity.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same filesystem tree or VS Code workspace
IF Roo Code is configured to send workspace context to a third-party model API
mitigations: Keep OpenBBTerminal data in a separate directory
Turn off file sharing between the agents
Redact financial and licensed data before Roo Code sees it
Use local-only model endpoints for Roo Code
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenBBTerminal supports multiple instances and uses filesystem/APIs, while Roo Code has unrestricted workspace write, shell, git, and filesystem access with shared state via filesystem. Concurrent writes to the same workspace or git state can overwrite each other or corrupt artifacts; the default Roo Code posture is especially risky. This is a high-confidence conflict pathway.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or git repository
IF Roo Code performs a write while OpenBBTerminal is reading or generating files
mitigations: Assign separate worktrees or directories
Pause one agent during the other’s write operations
Avoid shared git branches for concurrent edits
Use file locks for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can generate financial analyses that Roo Code may treat as input for code or documentation actions. Roo Code’s approval-per-tool default reduces but does not eliminate the chance it acts on unverified outputs. Because the pairwise handoff is plausible but not documented as authoritative, medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF Roo Code uses OpenBBTerminal output as a source of truth without independent verification
IF Roo Code then commits, edits, or executes based on that output
mitigations: Require Roo Code to cite source provenance before acting
Add a verification checklist for financial facts
Keep OpenBBTerminal outputs advisory only
Block direct commit or execution from unreviewed analysis
requires-engineering: insert a validation gate between agents

E_compliance.rationale: OpenBBTerminal explicitly touches financial and licensed data, while Roo Code handles source code and model-provider API keys. If regulated financial or licensed data is placed into a VS Code workspace, Roo Code’s broad filesystem access and external model calls can create retention or residency mismatches. The profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdiction mismatch, so medium fits.
conditions: IF regulated financial or licensed data is stored in the shared VS Code workspace
IF Roo Code forwards that workspace content to an external model provider
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the coding workspace
Use a local model for Roo Code
Review retention settings for the model provider
Separate secrets from project files
requires-engineering: implement data-class-based routing
